newsitem.title: KENYA: CRICKET-AFRIDI BREAKS RECORD FOR FASTEST CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AFRIDI BREAKS RECORD FOR FASTEST CENTURY.

text.p: Pakistan all rounder Shahid Afridi scored a century from 37 balls on Friday to break the world one-day international record at Nairobi Gymkhana.
Promoted to number three against Sri Lanka in an attempt to boost the run rate the 18-year-old Afridi pulverised the bowling with 11 sixes and six fours before finally falling for 102.
Afridi, playing in only his second international, missed the fastest one-day international 50 by one ball, but dipped under the previous century record by an 11 deliveries.
Both previous records were held by Sri Lanka's dynamic opener Sanath Jayasuriya who made 50 from 17 balls and 100 from 48 against Pakistan in a tournament in Singapore last April.

Afridi had the satisfaction of hammering Jayasuriya out of the bowling attack, taking 43 off the left arm spinner's two overs including five sixes. Afridi equalled Jayasuriya's record of 11 sixes in an innings.
Afridi made his debut against Kenya on Tuesday, but this was his first match against a top class international side.
